relevance_rank_note: Directly varies ApoE3 vs ApoE4 on primary rat cortical neurons and measures receptor surface/total levels by surface biotinylation, including internal null-control receptors and NHE6-based rescue of the recycling block.

description: Primary rat cortical neurons were pre-treated with naturally secreted ApoE3 or ApoE4 particles and then with Reelin to trigger Apoer2 endocytosis; surface biotinylation showed Apoer2 returned to the surface normally with ApoE3 but was strongly retained intracellularly with ApoE4. Effect is ApoE4 vs ApoE3 read off the bars; the stars compare each ApoE bar with the no-ApoE control, and ApoE4 vs ApoE3 is not tested.
quote: While Apoer2 quickly recycled in the presence of ApoE3, its reappearance on the cell surface was greatly delayed in the presence of ApoE4 (Figure 2B,C).
summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4) -> (less surface Apoer2 / delayed Apoer2 recycling)
system: Primary rat (Sprague-Dawley) cortical neurons, E18, DIV9-14; 30 min 5 ug/ml HEK293-secreted ApoE3 or ApoE4 particles, then 2 ug/ml Reelin 30 min; cell surface biotinylation, surface/total immunoblot. Rodent (rat) primary cortical neurons in vitro with exogenous human ApoE.
human_check: eff is the ApoE4 bar (~27) against the ApoE3 bar (~77) of normalized surface/total in Fig 2C. The *** bracket runs from control to ApoE4 and * from control to ApoE3; there is no ApoE3-ApoE4 bracket, so P is not shown (N/A). Changed from ~73% / <0.001 (vs no-ApoE control) at the team leader's approval, 2026-11-19 referee pass. Class 1 -> 3 (team leader, 2026-11-21): the assay triggers receptor internalisation with Reelin and then reads surface/total once, so it measures surface level (B'), not the recycling step itself.

description: In the same surface biotinylation experiment, the endocytic receptors Lrp1, Ldlr, insulin receptor and transferrin receptor showed comparable surface/total levels with ApoE3 and ApoE4, i.e. the ApoE4 surface-level defect was selective for Apoer2 and not a general block of receptor recycling. No significance mark or P value is given for these four receptors.
quote: By contrast, other endocytic cell surface receptors that do not bind ApoE, such as the insulin receptor (IR) or the transferrin receptor (TfR), or that do not interact with Reelin and therefore do not undergo ligand-induced endocytosis (low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (Lrp1) and low-density lipoprotein receptor (Ldlr)), were not significantly affected by the presence of ApoE
summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4) -> (no change in surface Lrp1, Ldlr, IR, TfR)
system: Primary rat (Sprague-Dawley) cortical neurons, E18, DIV9-14; 30 min 5 ug/ml ApoE3 or ApoE4 conditioned medium, then Reelin 2 ug/ml 30 min; surface biotinylation, surface/total immunoblot of Lrp1, Ldlr, IR, TfR. Rodent primary cortical neurons in vitro with exogenous human ApoE.
human_check: No significance markers sit on the Lrp1/Ldlr/IR/TfR bars in Fig 2C and no P value is printed for these null comparisons; all four bars sit at ~100 of the normalized control. The Discussion repeats the insulin receptor null: 'we did not detect impaired insulin receptor trafficking (Figure 2B and C)'. Class 1 -> 3 (team leader, 2026-11-21): the assay triggers receptor internalisation with Reelin and then reads surface/total once, so it measures surface level (B'), not the recycling step itself.

description: Pre-treating ApoE4-exposed neurons with the NHE inhibitor EMD87580 progressively restored Reelin-induced Apoer2 surface levels with increasing drug concentration, indicating the ApoE4 recycling block depends on endosomal pH.
quote: Increasing concentrations progressively restored normal surface recycling of Apoer2 in the presence of ApoE4 (Figure 4B,C).
summary: (ApoE4 + NHE inhibition) -> (surface Apoer2 restored to control level)
system: Primary rat (Sprague-Dawley) cortical neurons, E18, DIV9-14; 1 hr pre-incubation with EMD87580 at 0-3 uM, then 5 ug/ml ApoE4 conditioned medium and 2 ug/ml Reelin; surface biotinylation of Apoer2. Rodent primary cortical neurons in vitro with exogenous human ApoE and a pharmacological NHE inhibitor.
human_check: Rescue is dose-dependent (bars rise from ~23 at 0 uM to ~128 at 3 uM in Fig 4C), so a single effect size would misrepresent it. P code taken from the lowest-dose significant bracket (0.3 uM, **) under the legend key *p<0.05, **p<0.01, ***p<0.001; Fig 4C also shows *** at 1 uM and **** at 3 uM although the legend key lists no four-star level.

description: shRNA knockdown of vesicular Na+/H+ exchangers showed that only NHE6-directed shRNAs restored Apoer2 surface levels in ApoE4-treated neurons; shRNAs against NHE1, 5, 7, 8 or 9 had no effect, localising the ApoE4 recycling block to NHE6-dependent endosomal pH. No P is given: the stars in Fig 5D mark the ApoE4 loss after the non-NHE6 knockdowns, and the NHE6 rescue itself carries no test.
quote: None of the shRNAs directed against NHE1, 5, 7, 8 or 9 had any effect on surface Apoer2 expression, neither in the absence of ApoE4 or in its presence.
summary: (ApoE4 + NHE6 knockdown) -> (surface Apoer2 restored); (ApoE4 + NHE1/5/7/8/9 knockdown) -> (no change)
system: Primary rat (Sprague-Dawley) cortical neurons, E18, lentiviral shRNA against NHE1, 5, 6, 7, 8 or 9; then 5 ug/ml ApoE4 conditioned medium and 2 ug/ml Reelin; surface biotinylation of Apoer2. Rodent primary cortical neurons in vitro with exogenous human ApoE and shRNA manipulation.
human_check: P set to N/A: the *** in Fig 5D mark the persisting ApoE4 drop in non-NHE6 knockdowns (shNHE5, shNHE9), not the NHE6 rescue claimed here; the rescue itself carries no test. NHE1, 7 and 8 knockdowns are in Fig 5B. Legend test is a t-test.

description: With NHE6 knocked down by three independent shRNAs (or NHE inhibitor EMD87580), the ApoE4-induced loss of surface Apoer2 was abolished, while scrambled shRNA had no effect. The stars compare ApoE4 with control; the rescued bars are not tested against ApoE4, so no P is given.
quote: EMD87580 and the NHE6-specific shRNAs completely restored Apoer2 and glutamate receptor surface expression, while the scrambled shRNA had no effect
summary: (ApoE4) -> (less surface Apoer2); (ApoE4 + NHE6 knockdown) -> (surface Apoer2 restored)
system: Primary rat cortical neurons, E18, lentiviral shNHE6 (a, b, c; >90% NHE6 protein knockdown) or scrambled shRNA, or 3 uM EMD87580; 5 ug/ml ApoE4 conditioned medium plus 2 ug/ml Reelin; surface biotinylation of Apoer2, GluN2B, GluA1, GluA2/3. Rodent primary cortical neurons in vitro with exogenous human ApoE.
human_check: Split by panel at the team leader's approval (2026-11-19 referee pass). P is N/A: the *** compares the ApoE4 bars with control under Dunnett-style comparisons to control; rescued bars are never tested against ApoE4. Rescued bars carry no star.

description: Co-immunoprecipitation of Apoer2 from ApoE-treated neurons recovered more ApoE4 than ApoE3, indicating ApoE4 stays bound to Apoer2 in intracellular compartments longer, the proposed cause of the delayed recycling.
quote: The delayed recycling of Apoer2 was also apparent by the prolonged retention of cell-derived ApoE4 compared to cell-derived ApoE3 in Apoer2-containing intracellular compartments as shown by co-immunoprecipitation of neuronal lysates (Figure 2D,E).
summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4) -> (more ApoE retained on Apoer2 in intracellular compartments) -> (delayed recycling)
system: Primary rat cortical neurons, E18, treated 3 hr with 5 ug/ml ApoE3 or ApoE4 conditioned medium at 37C; anti-Apoer2 immunoprecipitation of lysates, ApoE immunoblot. Rodent primary cortical neurons in vitro with exogenous human ApoE.
human_check: Fig 2E plots relative ApoE levels as % of ApoE3: E3 set at ~100, E4 at ~158, hence ~1.6x; the authors print no number. The ** bracket is over the E3-vs-E4 pair (legend key **p<0.01, Student's t-test).
